thread:
liz: Heads-up: Enterprise POC with BankWave. They want Redwood Private deployed so traffic from their on-prem proxy hits our private service. Requirements: preserve client source IP for audit logs, strict egress allowlist, and minimal changes to their infra. Can we list tradeoffs (PrivateLink vs peering vs TGW) + a pasteable firewall snippet? POC start next week.

omar: TL;DR: PrivateLink = easiest security signoff but endpoint ENI becomes source IP (so network-layer src IP is lost). VPC Peering or Transit Gateway keeps the original 5-tuple intact. Peering = simpler for single VPC pair; TGW = better for multi-spoke.

chen: If they only need client identity for logging/siem, we can send X-Forwarded-For from our proxy and sign headers to prevent tampering. If they require raw TCP source IP at the application layer, only peering/TGW will work.

liz: Is Proxy Protocol an option? Customer asked about preserving IP without heavy routing changes.

omar: Proxy Protocol works if we own an L4 load balancer that terminates the connection and emits the original IP to the app. Options: NLB with proxy protocol -> app must support it. Still involves setup but avoids peering.

chen: Draft firewall allowlist (paste into their security questionnaire):
```
# Recommended outbound rules from on-prem/proxy to Redwood PrivateDeploy
# Prefer FQDN allowlist on corporate proxy
ALLOW tcp 443 to private.redwood-inference.net   # control plane & API
ALLOW tcp 443 to models.redwood-inference.net    # model pulls (can be scheduled)
ALLOW tcp 443 to telemetry.redwood-inference.net # optional metrics
# CIDR fallback if proxy does not support FQDNs (we will provide exact prefixes)
ALLOW tcp 443 to 198.51.100.0/22
```
Note: If they strictly TLS-inspect outbound, recommend adding our CN to inspection allowlist so SNI is preserved or use exception for our FQDN.

liz: Pricing question: at ~5TB/month which is cheaper? PrivateLink vs peering/TGW?

omar: Rough non-binding guidance:
- PrivateLink: per-endpoint-hour + per-GB processing. Ballpark $0.02-0.06/GB depending on region. Predictable but can be higher.
- Peering/TGW: typically lower per-GB egress in-region ($0.005-0.03/GB), but customer handles connectivity costs (DX, VPN) and ops overhead.
Summary: volume favors peering/TGW on cost; security/process favors PrivateLink.

chen: Add latency note: peering/TGW usually has lower p95 latency because it avoids the extra endpoint hop. If BankWave cares about inference latency we should include a small benchmark.

ops-bot: :white_check_mark: sandbox-bankwave provisioned in us-east-1 (sandbox-bankwave-01). Drive: https://drive.redwood/bankwave-poc (creds in secret manager).

liz: Next steps: omar will draft a one-page decision table + cost estimate. chen will produce the firewall snippet and pasteable questionnaire language about client identity and proxy-protocol options. Send to customer in 24h and schedule sync.

omar: Will do. I'll include CIDR change window and a recommended maintenance window for IP rotations.

chen: I'll include a short paragraph they can paste into their security doc: "Using PrivateLink results in endpoint ENI source IPs. We support X-Forwarded-For and Proxy Protocol to preserve client identity at the application level. For network-layer source IP preservation, configure cross-account VPC Peering or Transit Gateway. We will provide signed headers and audit logs for compliance."

liz: Thanks team.
